mechanism_explained: Nanomedicine is transport/biodistribution engineering; a particles fate is a dose-loss chain, so claims must rest on measured delivery.
The leaky vasculature that admits nanoparticles (EPR) also raises interstitial pressure, blocking deep penetration; drugs reach the rim, miss the core.
Platforms are problem-matched tools (Doxil cardiotoxicity, Abraxane solvent, PLGA release); benefit must be attributed precisely, not assumed from nano.
Passive EPR gets particles to the tumor (variable in humans); active ligands only improve uptake once there; the protein corona masks ligands.
An ADCs behavior is governed downstream of binding: linker stability, drug-to-antibody ratio, payload permeability (bystander effect).
Nano imagings main present value is biodistribution debugging - separating a delivery failure from a payload failure; signal is proxy, not proof.
One shared targeting molecule (PSMA, SSTR2) carries an imaging then a therapeutic isotope; emitter choice (beta crossfire vs alpha high-LET) matches geometry.
Most multifunctional particles have not translated while simpler designs have, because characterization/regulatory burden scales with complexity.
Nucleic-acid drugs act only if the vehicle (LNP via ionizable-lipid endosomal escape) delivers cargo to the cytosol; delivery is rate-limiting.
Light-activated therapy kills only where photosensitizer + correct-wavelength light + oxygen coincide; penetration and hypoxia bound it.
Nanoparticles are distributions not molecules; batch equivalence/characterization is the translation gate where most designs die.
The binding constraint is measured delivery and patient selection (image-then-treat), not new chemistry; successes measured, failures hoped.
